sn12.49:1.2: “Bhikkhus, an instructed noble disciple does not think:
sn12.49:1.4: ‘When what exists does what come to be? With the arising of what does what arise?
sn12.49:1.5: When what exists do volitional formations come to be? When what exists does consciousness come to be? When what exists does name-and-form come to be?… When what exists does aging-and-death come to be?’
sn12.49:2.1: “Rather, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple has knowledge about this that is independent of others:
sn12.49:2.2: ‘When this exists, that comes to be; with the arising of this, that arises.
sn12.49:2.3: When there is ignorance, volitional formations come to be.
sn12.49:2.4: When there are volitional formations, consciousness comes to be.
sn12.49:2.13: When there is birth, aging-and-death comes to be.’
sn12.49:2.15: ‘In such a way the world originates.’
sn12.49:3.1: “Bhikkhus, an instructed noble disciple does not think:
sn12.49:3.3: ‘When what does not exist does what not come to be? With the cessation of what does what cease?
sn12.49:3.4: When what does not exist do volitional formations not come to be? When what does not exist does consciousness not come to be? When what does not exist does name-and-form not come to be?… When what does not exist does aging-and-death not come to be?’”
sn12.49:4.1: “Rather, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple has knowledge about this that is independent of others:
sn12.49:4.2: ‘When this does not exist, that does not come to be; with the cessation of this, that ceases.
sn12.49:4.3: When there is no ignorance, volitional formations do not come to be.
sn12.49:4.4: When there are no volitional formations, consciousness does not come to be.
sn12.49:4.5: When there is no consciousness, name-and-form does not come to be….
sn12.49:4.9: aging-and-death does not come to be.’
sn12.49:4.11: ‘In such a way the world ceases.’
sn12.49:5.1: “Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple thus understands as they really are the origin and the passing away of the world, he is then called a noble disciple who is accomplished in view, accomplished in vision, who has arrived at this true Dhamma, who sees this true Dhamma, who possesses a trainee’s knowledge, a trainee’s true knowledge, who has entered the stream of the Dhamma, a noble one with penetrative wisdom, one who stands squarely before the door to the Deathless.”
